title: BehaviouralSpec
description: The canonical, language-independent DSL specification every Janus SDK's idiomatic layer implements (spec.md §3). One document, shared by every language; the style guide (spec.md §5) and the compatibility facade (spec.md §6) are per-language and per-primitive additions to it, not replacements.

primitives.description: One entry per user-facing DSL concept, language-independent.

Primitive.title: Primitive
Primitive.description: One DSL primitive, specified precisely enough to implement without reading another language's source (spec.md §3.3).

id.description: Stable kebab-case identifier, independent of any language's casing convention.

category.description: What kind of primitive this is (spec.md §3.1).

summary.description: One line: what a user reaches for this to do.

produces.description: What this primitive compiles to, structurally (spec.md §3.2) — an array because a primitive like 'execute' produces a sequence of protocol operations, not one document.

signature.description: Parameters named by role, not by per-language type (spec.md §3.2) — the concrete type is the style guide's business.

semantics.description: Precise behavioural prose, citing the owning design by section rather than restating it. Must clear the bar spec.md §3.3 states: implementable by someone who has never read another language's idiomatic layer.

errors.description: Structured protocol errors (engine-protocol spec §10) this primitive's translation must surface, and how.

conformance.description: Scenario ids in task 6.4's suite that exercise this primitive. Traceability only — this design does not define scenarios.

facade.description: Today's classic-DSL names this primitive replaces, and how (spec.md §6).

Produces.title: Produces
Produces.description: One thing this primitive compiles to. 'kind' selects which of the other members apply, following the same open-tag pattern as every other design's tagged documents.

operator.description: kind 'shape-operator': the shape-language operator name (design 2.2) this primitive emits a node for.

operation.description: kind 'protocol-operation': the engine-protocol operation name (design 2.1), e.g. 'consumer-session/add-interaction'.

path.description: kind 'spec-member': the member path within the interaction-spec document this primitive populates, e.g. 'parts.response.body'.

Param.title: Param
Param.description: One parameter, named by its role rather than its per-language type (spec.md §3.2).

ErrorSurface.title: ErrorSurface
ErrorSurface.description: One structured protocol error this primitive's translation must not swallow (spec.md §3.2).

code.description: An engine-protocol spec §10 error code, e.g. 'interaction-invalid'.

surfaced-as.description: How the idiomatic layer turns this into a language-native failure. Prose, not a type — the concrete exception/error type is the style guide's business.

FacadeMapping.title: FacadeMapping
FacadeMapping.description: One classic-DSL name this primitive replaces (spec.md §6.1). A 'kept' mapping MUST NOT change behaviour for any input that was legal before; 'adapted' and 'dropped' require 'reason' to say why.

from.description: The classic-DSL primitive (and its shape, if that disambiguates), e.g. 'term(generate, matcher)'.

reason.description: Required even for 'kept', where it can be short: why this is a lossless mapping, what default an 'adapted' mapping supplies, or what a 'dropped' primitive's migration path is (spec.md §6.1).
